title: eludite.debug.attach input
description: Debug > Attach to Process... (Ctrl+Alt+P): debug a process that is already running, by `pid` or `process_name` (eludite.debug.processes lists the candidates with their runtime and whether Eludite started them), or a web page by `tab` or `url` (brief 0038). The debug adapter follows the process's runtime unless `adapter` names one: `dotnet` (a `dotnet <app>.dll` process) attaches with netcoredbg by process id; `mono` attaches with eludite-dbg-mono to the debugger agent the program was started with (`mono --debug --debugger-agent=transport=dt_socket,server=y,address=127.0.0.1:PORT`, read from its command line, or `mono`): Mono has no late attach, so a Mono program started without an agent cannot be attached; `native` attaches with lldb-dap by process id. On Windows a .NET Framework process (`netfx`) is refused until eludite-dbg-netfx (brief 0004) exists. The session goes through mode `launching` to `running` (`break` when the adapter stops it at once) with `session.attached` true and no build; every debugger window, key and command then works as for a launch. Stop (eludite.debug.stop, Shift+F5) detaches: the process keeps running, and the status bar says so. Restart is refused for an attached session. Refused while a debugging session runs; the program of Start Without Debugging (Ctrl+F5) may be attached to. Without `pid` or `process_name`, from the UI, the Attach to Process dialog opens; an agent must name the process. Permission class execute for a process Eludite started (`launched_by_eludite`: Ctrl+F5's or F5's program and its child processes), dangerous for any other one; the solution policy's `debug.attach` or `debug.drive` set to `deny` refuses agents. The answer is the stop summary (debug-stop-summary.output.json): where and why it stopped, the top frames, the top frame's locals and the watches within the budget parameters, and the program's output since `output_since`; on a timeout `mode` is `running` (or `launching`, `building`), and after the session ends `design` with `exit_code` and `message`. A page is debugged with vscode-js-debug (`adapter: javascript`, implied by `tab` and `url`; refused with `pid` or `process_name`, since a browser is attached by tab or url): `tab` is a tab of Eludite's browser (eludite.browser.tabs' `id`, the Web Browser window's tabs; eludite.debug.processes lists them under `tabs`), attached through the engine's remote debugging port on 127.0.0.1; `url` is a page of the browser Eludite runs, or a Chrome DevTools websocket url (`ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/page/<id>`) of a Chrome started with `--remote-debugging-port`. vscode-js-debug and Node are located on the machine, never bundled (tools/js-debug/fetch.sh; the settings debugger.jsDebugPath and debugger.nodePath; protocol/schemas/dap-js-debug.md). The browser session is `attached`, named after the tab's title (renamed when the title changes), `runtime` `javascript`; js-debug starts a child session per page target (DAP `startDebugging`), listed under it with `parent`: breakpoints in `.js`, `.mjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.vue` and `.svelte` files bind there through the page's source maps, and every eludite.debug.* command works on it by `session`. Stop on the browser session detaches (its children end with it) and leaves the page running; the tab closing ends the session with `design` and a message. Permission class execute for a `tab` (the browser Eludite runs), dangerous for a `url`.
x-eludite-escalates: Dangerous for a `url` (a page of a browser Eludite may not have started), and when the process is not one Eludite started (`launched_by_eludite` false in eludite.debug.processes, or a `process_name` no started process has), and whenever the solution's policy sets `debug.drive` to `prompt`; refused for agents when the policy sets `debug.attach` or `debug.drive` to `deny`.

pid.description: The process id, as eludite.debug.processes lists it.

process_name.description: The process's name (`dotnet`, `mono`, `MyService`; the extension may be left out), compared without regard to case. Exactly one process must have it; otherwise the command is refused and lists the matching processes with their ids, so pass `pid`. Ignored when `pid` is given.

tab.description: A tab of Eludite's browser to debug its page's JavaScript with vscode-js-debug: eludite.browser.tabs' `id` (`t1`), the tab a web project's launch opened (eludite.debug.state's `session.browser.tab`), or one eludite.debug.processes lists under `tabs`. Not with `pid`, `process_name` or `url`.

url.description: A page to debug with vscode-js-debug: an http(s) url of a tab of the browser Eludite runs (the first tab showing it), or the Chrome DevTools websocket url of a page of a Chrome started with `--remote-debugging-port` (`ws://HOST:PORT/devtools/page/<id>`, as its `/json/list` names it). Not with `pid`, `process_name` or `tab`.

adapter.description: The debug adapter: `coreclr` (netcoredbg), `mono` (eludite-dbg-mono), `netfx` (eludite-dbg-netfx, Windows only, not built yet: refused), `lldb` (lldb-dap) or `javascript` (vscode-js-debug, for a `tab` or `url`; refused with `pid` or `process_name`). Default: from the process's runtime (`dotnet`: coreclr, `mono`: mono, `native`: lldb, `netfx`: netfx), and `javascript` for a `tab` or `url`. A process of runtime `unknown` needs it.

transport.description: Reach a debug adapter already listening elsewhere instead of starting one here (ADR-0007): `{"kind": "tcp", "host", "port"}`. The process id is then the remote machine's; eludite.debug.processes lists this machine's processes only.

mono.description: Where a Mono program's debugger agent listens, for `adapter` `mono`: `address` (default 127.0.0.1) and `port`. Default: read from the process's `--debugger-agent=...,address=HOST:PORT,...,server=y` option.

web_root.description: For a `tab` or `url`: the folder the page's urls map to (vscode-js-debug's `webRoot`), so breakpoints in source files bind and frames name them through the page's source maps. Default: the `wwwroot` folder of the project whose launch opened the tab (else that project's folder), else the open solution's or folder's.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the session to start (the adapter attached and the debuggee running or stopped) before answering, in milliseconds. From the UI the command never waits; from another thread (an agent) the default is 5000. An answer with mode `launching` means the attach is still under way; call eludite.debug.wait later.

depth.description: How many levels of the locals to expand: 1 (default) lists the top level only; up to 5. Expansion is breadth-first and stops when `max_variables` rows are listed.

max_variables.description: The most variable rows listed, counting every level (default 50, at most 500).

max_value_chars.description: Values longer than this are cut and end with `… (N chars)`, the row saying `value_truncated` (default 200, at most 10000).

max_frames.description: The most stack frames listed (default 10, at most 200); page further with eludite.debug.stack.

max_output_lines.description: The most program output lines listed (default 20, at most 1000; 0 lists none).

output_since.description: An output cursor (`output.next` of an earlier answer, or eludite.debug.output's `next`): list the program's lines from it on. Default: the last `max_output_lines` lines.
